medkg_search.description:
Hybrid search (dense + lexical + rerank) over 236k Q1 medical-AI papers or their full-text chunks.
Returns ranked hits with work_id, title, year, journal, Q1 flag, DOI and snippet; filters narrow by year/Q1/journal/entities.

query.description: Natural-language or keyword query over the corpus

mode.description: hybrid = dense (Qdrant) + lexical (FTS5) fused by RRF, then reranked

scope.description: Search paper abstracts or full-text chunks

rerank.description: Apply the bge-reranker to the fused candidates

is_q1.description: Restrict to Q1-journal papers (true) or non-Q1 (false)

journal.description: Journal name substring filter, e.g. 'Scientific Reports'

modality.description: Modality entity filter, e.g. MRI, CT, histopathology

task.description: Task entity filter, e.g. segmentation, prognosis

method.description: AI-method entity filter, e.g. transformer, U-Net

medkg_get_paper.description:
Fetch one paper: metadata, MeSH/topics/entities, graph neighbours (cites, cited-by, similar) and chunk count.
Optionally returns the full-text chunks (section filter available) for grounding a claim in the paper's body.

work_id.description: Corpus work_id, e.g. PMC10686892 or DOI:10.1038/s41598-026-58823-1 (a bare DOI/PMCID also resolves)

include_chunks.description: Also fetch the full-text chunks of the paper

section.description: When include_chunks, keep only chunks whose section matches (substring)

medkg_graph_neighbors.description:
Return the Neo4j neighbourhood (nodes + edges) of one node for graph exploration or a UI graph view.
Works for papers (work_id) and ontology entities (Method/Task/Modality/Dataset/MeSH/Journal by name or id).

label.description: Node label: Paper, Journal, Author, MeSH, Topic, Keyword, Method, Task, Modality, Dataset, Metric, Organ, Disease

key.description: Node key: work_id for Paper, name for entities, ui for MeSH, issn/name for Journal

medkg_cypher.description:
Run a read-only Cypher query against the MedKG Neo4j graph (30 s timeout, READ access mode enforced server-side).
Use it for ad-hoc counts, joins across Paper/Method/Task/Modality/MeSH/Journal nodes and citation paths.

query.description: Read-only Cypher (MATCH/RETURN/WITH/CALL db.* ...). CREATE/MERGE/SET/DELETE/REMOVE/DROP, CALL {} IN TRANSACTIONS and apoc write procedures are rejected

medkg_answer.description:
Evidence-grounded answer: hybrid retrieval + rerank, Neo4j graph expansion, then LLM synthesis citing only retrieved items [n].
Returns the markdown answer, the [n] -> work_id citation map, the evidence passages and an insufficient_evidence flag.

question.description: Research question to answer from the corpus with numbered citations

k.description: Evidence items retrieved before graph expansion (1-60)

scope.description: Retrieve full-text chunks (default, falls back to abstracts while the chunk index builds) or abstracts

style.description: Answer style: direct evidence answer, related-work prose, or gap statements

medkg_related_work.description:
Build a related-work table (work_id, title, year, journal, Q1, method, modality, dataset, metric values, summary).
Rows come from hybrid retrieval; entities come from the graph/lexicon and the LLM reads only each abstract.

topic.description: Topic of the related-work section, e.g. 'transformer-based brain tumour MRI segmentation'

k.description: Number of papers in the table (1-100)

summarise.description: Let the LLM extract method/modality/dataset/metrics and a one-sentence summary per row

medkg_gaps.description:
Graph-grounded research-gap analysis: Method x Task x Modality cell counts, sparse/empty cells, yearly trend, Q1 journals.
Returns the statistics plus a cited markdown analysis (LLM) so a gap can be turned into a paper idea.

topic.description: Research topic to analyse for gaps, e.g. 'federated learning for histopathology'

synthesise.description: Let the LLM write the gap narrative from the graph statistics

medkg_q1_guideline.description:
Return the Q1 acceptance guideline v7 (14 hard gates, 14 strong signals, section blueprint, claim rules, per-journal deltas).
Optionally narrow to one section or one journal profile; graph_items reports how many guideline nodes exist in Neo4j.

section.description: Return only one section: hard_gates, strong_signals, section_blueprint, abstract_template, claim_rules, rejection_reasons, per_journal, checklist, summary

journal_key.description: With section=per_journal (or alone): one journal profile, e.g. scientific_reports

medkg_q1_evidence.description:
Find supporting and contradicting passages for a claim (Q1 claim-discipline check).
Each passage carries work_id, section, score, stance and rationale; insufficient_evidence flags weak retrieval.

claim.description: A manuscript claim to audit, e.g. 'External validation improves generalisation of CT-based lung nodule classifiers'

classify.description: Let the LLM label each passage supports/contradicts/neutral with a rationale

medkg_q1_journal_fit.description:
Rank Q1 target journals for an abstract using accepted-paper similarity, topic/MeSH overlap and per-journal deltas.
Each row lists similar accepted work_ids, SJR, submission profile (abstract/word limits) and what that journal rewards.

medkg_stats.description:
Report MedKG health and build status: Neo4j node/edge counts, Qdrant/FTS index sizes, LLM provider, index progress.
Use it first to see whether the graph and indexes are fully loaded before relying on graph-heavy tools.

medsam_segment_with_box.description:
Segment one or more targets in a 2D medical image from bounding-box prompts with MedSAM ViT-B.
Input is an image (or test_demo-style npz) plus xyxy boxes; output is a uint8 label map (label i+1 for box i), per-box masks and an overlay figure.

image_path.description: Path to a 2D medical image (png/jpg/jpeg/tif/tiff/bmp; grey or RGB, an alpha channel is dropped, >8-bit intensities are min-max scaled to 0-255) or to an .npz with key 'imgs' (H,W,3) uint8 and optionally 'boxes' (N,4).

boxes.description: Bounding boxes [[x_min, y_min, x_max, y_max], ...] in original pixel coordinates (0 <= x_min < x_max <= width, 0 <= y_min < y_max <= height); None uses the 'boxes' key of an .npz input.

checkpoint_path.description: MedSAM ViT-B checkpoint (.pth); None resolves medsam_vit_b.pth under MEDSAM_CHECKPOINT_DIR (default <package>/data/MedSAM_checkpoints).

device.description: 'auto' picks the CUDA device with the most free memory if at least 4 GiB is free, else CPU.

output_dir.description: Base output directory (default MEDSAM_OUTPUT_DIR or <package>/tmp/outputs); a fresh subdirectory is created per call.

medsam_segment_3d_with_box.description:
Segment 3D targets in a CT/MR volume from 3D bounding boxes by running MedSAM slice by slice with the script's box propagation.
Input is a volume (npz 'imgs' or nii/nii.gz/mha/nrrd) plus boxes [x_min,y_min,z_min,x_max,y_max,z_max] (z_max exclusive); output is a label volume npz (+ nii.gz for image i

volume_path.description: 3D volume: a MedSAM npz with 'imgs' (D,H,W) uint8 (optional 'spacing' (x,y,z) and 'boxes' (N,6)), or a SimpleITK-readable CT/MR image (nii, nii.gz, mha, nrrd) that gets the script's whole-volume min-max scaling to uint8 (optionally clipped); no MR percentile normalisation is applied, so run medsam_preprocess_ct_mr first for MR images.

boxes_3d.description: 3D boxes [[x_min, y_min, z_min, x_max, y_max, z_max], ...] in voxel indices of the (D,H,W) array (x = column, y = row, z = slice), z_max exclusive; box i becomes label i+1 (later labels overwrite overlaps); empty uses the npz 'boxes' array.

propagate_boxes.description: True: give the box only to the seed slice z_min + (z_max-1 - z_min)//2 and propagate it with the script's loops (bounding box of the previous slice's mask, or the given box if that mask is empty); False: apply the given box on every slice of the z-range without propagation.

bbox_shift.description: Margin in 1024-grid pixels added around the previous slice's mask when propagating (script get_bbox default 5); unused when propagate_boxes is False.

clip_intensities.description: Clip intensities to [clip_lower, clip_upper] before the min-max scaling (the script's commented-out CT window line); False = no clipping, as the script runs (for uint8 MedSAM npz volumes leave False).

clip_lower.description: Lower intensity bound used when clip_intensities is True (script's commented-out CT soft-tissue window: -160 HU, i.e. WL 40 / WW 400 as in pre_CT_MR.py).

clip_upper.description: Upper intensity bound used when clip_intensities is True (script's commented-out CT soft-tissue window: 240 HU).

checkpoint_path.description: MedSAM ViT-B checkpoint (medsam_vit_b.pth); empty resolves it from MEDSAM_CHECKPOINT_DIR (fallback <package>/data/MedSAM_checkpoints).

device.description: Compute device; 'auto' picks the CUDA device with the most free memory if at least 4 GiB are free, else CPU.

output_dir.description: Base output directory (empty = MEDSAM_OUTPUT_DIR or <package>/tmp/outputs); a fresh subdirectory is created per call.

medsam_segment_with_point.description:
Segment an abdominal organ in a 2-D CT slice from single positive clicks with MedSAM's EXPERIMENTAL FLARE22 point-prompt model (decoder fine-tuned only for 13 organs: liver, kidneys, spleen, pancreas, aorta, IVC, adrenal glands, gallbladder, esophagus, stomach, duodenum).
Input is a png/jpg, MedSAM

image_path.description: 2-D image (.png/.jpg, grey or RGB), a MedSAM .npz with 'imgs' ((H,W), (H,W,3) or (D,H,W) uint8), or a CT .nii/.nii.gz volume (HU; windowed as in the notebook)

points.description: Positive clicks [[x, y], ...] in pixel coordinates of the image as passed to the model (x = column, y = row; for nii inputs with apply_notebook_rotation the 180-degree-rotated frame); one mask per click, label 1 (foreground)

slice_index.description: Slice (0-based, first axis) for .nii/.npz volumes; default the notebook's middle slice int(D/2); must be omitted for 2-D inputs

window_min.description: Lower CT window bound in HU applied to nii volumes before volume-wise min-max scaling to uint8 (notebook: -240)

window_max.description: Upper CT window bound in HU for nii volumes (notebook: 160)

apply_notebook_rotation.description: nii inputs only: rotate the slice by 180 degrees (np.rot90(slice, 2)) as the notebook does before set_image; clicks and masks are then in that rotated frame. Ignored for png/npz

checkpoint_path.description: Path or file name of the point-prompt checkpoint (default medsam_point_prompt_flare22.pth, resolved in MEDSAM_CHECKPOINT_DIR or <package>/data/MedSAM_checkpoints)

device.description: auto = CUDA device with the most free memory if >= 4 GiB free, else CPU

output_dir.description: Base output directory; a fresh subdirectory is created per call (default MEDSAM_OUTPUT_DIR or <package>/tmp/outputs)

medsam_segment_with_text.description:
Segment FLARE22 abdominal organs in a 2D CT slice from organ-name text prompts with MedSAM's experimental CLIP text-prompt model (fixed 13-organ vocabulary, FLARE22-trained decoder).
Input is a 2D image or a CT volume plus a slice index and a list of organ names; output is one binary mask per prompt

image_path.description: 2D image (PNG/JPG/BMP/TIF; .npy or .npz key 'imgs' shaped (H,W) or (H,W,3)) or a CT volume (.nii/.nii.gz/.mha/.mhd/.nrrd read with SimpleITK and HU-windowed; .npy/.npz 'imgs' shaped (D,H,W) uint8) whose slice is chosen with slice_index

prompts.description: Organ names from the checkpoint's FLARE22 vocabulary, matched after lower().strip(): liver, right kidney, spleen, pancreas, aorta, inferior vena cava (ivc), right adrenal gland (rag), left adrenal gland (lag), gallbladder, esophagus, stomach, duodenum, left kidney

slice_index.description: 0-based index along the first array axis for 3D inputs; None selects the notebook's middle slice int(D/2); must be None for 2D inputs

window_min.description: Lower bound of the notebook's CT window for SimpleITK volumes (HU; clip, then min-max to uint8 over the whole volume)

window_max.description: Upper bound of the notebook's CT window for SimpleITK volumes (HU)

apply_notebook_rotation.description: For SimpleITK volumes, draw the overlay PNG rotated by 180 degrees (np.rot90(., 2)) as the notebook displays these slices; masks are always saved in array orientation

checkpoint_path.description: Text-prompt checkpoint (default medsam_text_prompt_flare22.pth); a bare file name is resolved inside MEDSAM_CHECKPOINT_DIR

medsam_checkpoint_path.description: Base MedSAM ViT-B checkpoint (default medsam_vit_b.pth) that the notebook uses to instantiate the architecture before every weight is overwritten from checkpoint_path

device.description: auto = CUDA device with the most free memory if at least 4 GiB is free, else CPU

output_dir.description: Base output directory (default MEDSAM_OUTPUT_DIR or <package>/tmp/outputs); a fresh subdirectory is created per call

medsam_evaluate_dsc_nsd.description:
Score a predicted label map against a reference label map with the MedSAM paper's metrics (per-label DSC and NSD at a surface tolerance, default 2 mm) using utils/SurfaceDice.py.
Inputs: two label-map files (npz/npy/png/nii; 2D maps are scored as one slice with unit spacing, 3D maps with spacing_mm

prediction_path.description: Predicted label map: .npz (array 'segs' by default), .npy, .png/.bmp/.tif label image, or .nii/.nii.gz/.mha/.nrrd

ground_truth_path.description: Reference label map in the same shape and format family (.npz array 'gts' by default, .npy, image, or nii)

prediction_key.description: Array name holding the prediction inside an .npz file

ground_truth_key.description: Array name holding the reference inside an .npz file

labels.description: Label ids to score (each must occur in the reference); default = every non-zero reference label

spacing_mm.description: Voxel spacing in ARRAY-AXIS order (z,y,x for a (D,H,W) map; 2 or 3 values for 2D); default: nii header or npz 'spacing' converted to array order, else [1,1,1]

npz_spacing_order.description: Axis order of an npz 'spacing' triple: MedSAM npz files store (x,y,z) for (z,y,x) arrays, so 'xyz' reverses it to array order; 'zyx' uses it as stored

tolerance_mm.description: Surface tolerance tau for NSD in mm (pixels for 2D); the paper uses 2

include_asd_hd95.description: Also report average surface distance (gt->pred, pred->gt) and the 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance

output_dir.description: Base output directory; a fresh subdirectory is created per call (default: MEDSAM_OUTPUT_DIR or <package>/tmp/outputs)

medsam_preprocess_ct_mr.description: Convert a CT or MR volume into MedSAM's uint8 (D,H,W) npz input format with the paper's CT window (level/width) or MR 0.5-99.5 percentile normalisation (pre_CT_MR.py); an optional label_path enables the script's label branch (remove_label_ids, default [12]; tumor_id instances; cc3d.dust voxel thresh

image_path.description: 3D CT or MR volume file (nii/nii.gz or any SimpleITK-readable format); a scalar (D,H,W) image, e.g. FLARE22 *_0000.nii.gz

modality.description: CT: clip to window_level +/- window_width/2 then min-max to [0,255]; MR: clip to the 0.5/99.5 percentiles of voxels > 0, min-max, background (== 0) kept at 0 (utils/README applies this branch to MR, ultrasound, mammography and OCT)

window_level.description: CT only: window level in HU (README/paper soft-tissue default 40; utils/README alternatives: chest -600, brain 40; the extension notebooks use -40 for FLARE22)

window_width.description: CT only: window width in HU (soft tissue 400; chest 1500; brain 80)

label_path.description: Optional ground-truth label volume with the same (D,H,W) shape (integer labels, 0 = background). When given, the script's label branch runs (label-id removal, tumour instances, cc3d.dust thresholds, crop to non-empty slices, 'gts' saved). This branch is extracted verbatim but NOT verified against reference data (no FLARE22 label was available).

remove_label_ids.description: Label ids set to 0 before cleaning (only with label_path). None = the script default [12] (FLARE22 duodenum); pass [] to keep every label.

tumor_id.description: Only with label_path: semantic label to convert into 26-connected instance labels (ids max_label+1...), as the script does for multiple tumours

voxel_num_thre2d.description: Only with label_path: per-slice objects with fewer pixels than this are removed (cc3d.dust, 8-connectivity); script default 100

voxel_num_thre3d.description: Only with label_path: 3D objects with fewer voxels than this are removed (cc3d.dust, 26-connectivity); script default 1000

save_slices_1024.description: Also write the script's per-slice training files: imgs/<stem>-NNN.npy float64 (1024,1024,3) in [0,1] (order-3 resize) and, with label_path, gts/<stem>-NNN.npy uint8 (1024,1024) (order-0). About 25 MB and 1 s per slice (2.3 GB for 93 slices), hence off by default.

save_sanity_nii.description: Write the script's sanity nii.gz copies (<stem>_img.nii.gz[, _gt]; no geometry, as in the script) plus geometry-preserving copies (<stem>_img_with_geometry.nii.gz[, _gt])

output_dir.description: Base output directory; a fresh subdirectory is created per call (default: env MEDSAM_OUTPUT_DIR or <package>/tmp/outputs)

cellpose_segment_image.description:
Segment cells or nuclei in a 2D image with a pretrained Cellpose model (notebooks/run_cellpose.ipynb).
Input is an image file; outputs are label masks (png/tif/npy), a GUI-loadable _seg.npy, ImageJ outlines, raw flows (npz) and the 4-panel segmentation figure.

image_path.description: Path of a 2D image (png/jpg/tif; grayscale, RGB or a small channel-first tif)

model_type.description: Built-in Cellpose model; cyto/cyto2/nuclei also ship a size model for diameter estimation

pretrained_model_path.description: Path of a custom/user-trained Cellpose model file; overrides model_type when given

channels.description: [cytoplasm, nucleus] channels: 0=grayscale/none, 1=red, 2=green, 3=blue (e.g. [0,0] grayscale, [2,3] green cells + blue nuclei)

diameter.description: Mean object diameter in pixels; None estimates it with the size model (cyto/cyto2/nuclei) or uses the model's training diameter for other models

flow_threshold.description: Maximum allowed flow error per mask (higher keeps more masks); not used in 3D

cellprob_threshold.description: Cell probability threshold in (-6, 6); decrease to find more and larger masks

net_avg.description: Average the 4 built-in networks (cyto/cyto2/nuclei; the CLI default) instead of running one network

resample.description: Run the flow dynamics at the original image size (slower, more accurate boundaries)

device.description: Compute device; auto picks the CUDA device with the most free memory (>= 4 GiB) else CPU

output_dir.description: Base output directory; a fresh per-call subdirectory is created (default: CELLPOSE_OUTPUT_DIR or <package>/tmp/outputs)

cellpose_estimate_diameter.description:
Estimate the mean object diameter of a 2D image with the Cellpose size model (models.SizeModel.eval).
Input is an image file; output is the two-step diameter estimate (style regression, then median mask size) in pixels.

model_type.description: Built-in model whose size model is used (cyto/cyto2: 30 px mean, nuclei: 17 px)

device.description: Compute device; auto picks the CUDA device with the most free memory (>= 4 GiB) else CPU

output_dir.description: Optional base output directory; when given a fresh subdirectory with a JSON record is written, otherwise no files are produced

cellpose_segment_3d.description:
Segment a 3D image stack with Cellpose, either with true 3D flows (do_3D) or by stitching 2D masks (notebooks/run_cellpose_GPU.ipynb).
Input is a tif/npy volume; outputs are the (Z,Y,X) label volume (npy/tif), _seg.npy, raw flows, per-plane and per-label count CSVs and plane overlay figures.

image_path.description: Path of a 3D tif/tiff stack (Z x Y x X, Z x C x Y x X or Z x Y x X x C) or an .npy volume

model_type.description: Built-in Cellpose model (cyto/cyto2/nuclei may use the 4-net ensemble via net_avg)

pretrained_model_path.description: Path of a custom/user-trained Cellpose model file; overrides model_type when given

channels.description: [cytoplasm, nucleus] channels: 0=grayscale/none, 1=red, 2=green, 3=blue (e.g. [2,1] green cells + red nuclei)

diameter.description: Object diameter in pixels (set it: no size estimation in 3D); None uses the model's built-in mean diameter (30 px cyto-type, 17 px nuclei)

mode.description: do_3D: 2D flows from XY/XZ/YZ slices combined into 3D masks; stitch: 2D masks per plane stitched by IoU >= stitch_threshold

stitch_threshold.description: IoU threshold for stitching masks across planes (stitch mode only, must be > 0)

anisotropy.description: Z sampling factor relative to XY for do_3D (e.g. 2.0 if Z is sampled half as densely); None = isotropic

channel_axis.description: Axis of the channel dimension in the stack; None lets Cellpose infer it (smallest axis)

z_axis.description: Axis of the Z dimension in the stack; None lets Cellpose infer it

flow_threshold.description: Maximum allowed flow error per mask (stitch mode only; ignored by do_3D)

cellprob_threshold.description: Cell probability threshold in (-6, 6); decrease to find more and larger masks

net_avg.description: Average the 4 built-in networks (cyto/cyto2/nuclei only) instead of one network

device.description: Compute device; auto picks the CUDA device with the most free memory (>= 4 GiB) else CPU

output_dir.description: Base output directory; a fresh per-call subdirectory is created (default: CELLPOSE_OUTPUT_DIR or <package>/tmp/outputs)

cellpose_suggest_model.description:
Suggest the best model-zoo Cellpose model for an image from its style vector, as the GUI 'suggest model' button does (gui.py L1917-1938).
Input is an image file; output is the suggested model name with its 5 nearest training-style neighbours (Leiden cluster labels and distances).

image_path.description: Path of an image (png/jpg/tif); for stacks the middle plane is used as in the GUI

diameter.description: Object diameter in pixels used to rescale the image before computing its style (GUI default 30)

device.description: Compute device; auto picks the CUDA device with the most free memory (>= 4 GiB) else CPU

output_dir.description: Optional base output directory; when given a fresh subdirectory with a JSON record and the style vector is written

cellpose_train_model.description:
Fine-tune a pretrained Cellpose model (or train from scratch) on a folder of images with label masks, the Cellpose 2.0 human-in-the-loop recipe.
Input is a training folder (+ optional test folder) of image/label pairs; output is the trained model file, diam_labels, per-epoch losses, the upstream log

train_dir.description: Folder of training images (.tif/.tiff/.png/.jpg) with a label file per image: <stem>_seg.npy (Cellpose GUI) or <stem>_masks.tif/.png (label image, 0=background)

test_dir.description: Optional folder of test images with labels in the same format; used for the test loss during training and for the notebook's average-precision check after training

mask_filter.description: Label file convention: '_seg.npy' (GUI files, notebook default) or '_masks' (<stem>_masks.tif/.tiff/.png)

initial_model.description: Pretrained model-zoo network to fine-tune (downloaded on first use) or 'scratch' for random initialisation; ignored when pretrained_model_path is given

pretrained_model_path.description: Path of a custom Cellpose model file to continue training from (e.g. a model produced by this tool); overrides initial_model

channels.description: [channel to segment, nuclear channel]: 0=grayscale/none, 1=red, 2=green, 3=blue; notebook uses [2, 1] (green cytoplasm, red nuclei)

learning_rate.description: Peak SGD learning rate, ramped up linearly over the first 10 epochs (notebook: 0.1); scalar only

nimg_per_epoch.description: Minimum number of images sampled per epoch (notebook: 8, useful for small training sets); null = upstream default (each image once per epoch)

model_name.description: File name of the trained model, written to <output>/train/models/<model_name>

seed.description: Seed for python/numpy/torch RNGs with deterministic cuDNN/cuBLAS for the call (bit-identical replays on the same GPU); the value only changes the random initialisation of 'scratch' (upstream training reseeds numpy itself, so fine-tuning a pretrained model gives the same result for every seed); null = upstream behaviour (numpy seeded by cellpose, torch unseeded, non-deterministic cuDNN)

device.description: 'auto' = CUDA device with the most free memory (>= 4 GiB) else CPU; note CPU and GPU compute different flow targets, so results differ between device classes

output_dir.description: Base output directory; a fresh subdirectory is created per call

cellpose_evaluate_masks.description:
Score predicted label masks against ground truth with Cellpose's average precision AP = TP/(TP+FP+FN) at IoU thresholds and the aggregated Jaccard index.
Input is a predicted and a ground-truth mask file (or matched folders); output is per-image AP/TP/FP/FN per threshold, AJI, their means and CSV/JS

pred_masks_path.description: Predicted label masks: one file (_seg.npy, .npy, .tif/.tiff/.png label image) or a folder of '<stem><pred_mask_filter>[.ext]' files

true_masks_path.description: Ground-truth label masks in the same formats: one file, or a folder of '<stem><true_mask_filter>[.ext]' files matched to the predictions by stem

pred_mask_filter.description: Suffix selecting prediction files inside a folder, e.g. '_cp_masks' (Cellpose outputs; one file per stem, tif preferred over png), '_cp_masks.png', '_seg.npy', '_masks'; '' = every .npy/.tif/.tiff/.png file

true_mask_filter.description: Suffix selecting ground-truth files inside a folder, e.g. '_seg.npy' (GUI labels), '_masks'; '' = every .npy/.tif/.tiff/.png file

thresholds.description: IoU thresholds for the matching (paper/notebook default [0.5, 0.75, 0.9])

output_dir.description: Base output directory; a fresh subdirectory is created per call

cellpose_masks_to_rois.description:
Export a Cellpose (or any) 2D label mask to ImageJ/Fiji ROIs, outline text, label PNG/TIF and per-object sizes.
Input is a mask file path (_seg.npy / .npy / .png / .tif); output is a fresh directory with the selected files plus object counts and the median diameter.

masks_path.description: Path to a 2D label mask: a Cellpose `_seg.npy` (key 'masks'), a `.npy` integer label array, or a `.png`/`.tif` label image (0 = background, 1..N = object ids).

imagej_rois.description: Write `<base>_rois.zip`, a native ImageJ/Fiji ROI-manager archive with one FREEHAND .roi per object (cellpose.io.save_rois semantics).

outlines_txt.description: Write `<base>_cp_outlines.txt`, the legacy ImageJ outline list (one line per object: x0,y0,x1,y1,... for imagej_roi_converter.py) via cellpose.io.outlines_to_text.

masks_png.description: Write `<base>_cp_masks.png` (16-bit label PNG) via cellpose.io.save_masks(png=True); skipped by Cellpose when the mask has no objects or more than 65535 labels.

per_object_csv.description: Write `<base>_object_stats.csv` with, per label: area_px (pixel count), sqrt_area and equivalent_diameter_px from cellpose.utils.diameters, n_outline_vertices, centroid_y_px/centroid_x_px (mean pixel coordinates) and the ROI name assigned in the zip.

output_dir.description: Base output directory; a fresh `cellpose_masks_to_rois_<timestamp>_<id>/` subdirectory is created per call (default: $CELLPOSE_OUTPUT_DIR or <package>/tmp/outputs).

medmnist_describe_dataset.description:
Describe the MedMNIST v2 dataset registry: list all 18 datasets or return the full record of one dataset flag.
Input is an optional flag; output is registry metadata (task, label map, channels, split sizes, image sizes, licence, download URL/MD5, local npz files) plus an optional JSON artifact.

flag.description: MedMNIST dataset flag such as 'pathmnist' or 'organmnist3d' (case-insensitive; the class name 'PathMNIST' is accepted); omit or leave empty to list all 18 datasets

data_root.description: Directory holding MedMNIST npz files, used only to report which sizes are already present locally; default env MEDMNIST_DATA_ROOT or <package>/data/medmnist

medmnist_evaluate_predictions.description:

output_dir.description: Base directory for this call's logs; a fresh subdirectory is created (default <project>/tmp/outputs or $NNUNET_OUTPUT_DIR)

nnunet_plot_overlay_pngs.description:
Render one QC PNG per training case showing the slice with the most foreground with the label map blended in colour (nnUNetv2_plot_overlay_pngs; spacing is disregarded, 3D images only).

nnunet_apply_postprocessing.description:
Apply a determined nnU-Net postprocessing (e.g. keep only the largest connected component of the foreground / of single labels) to every label map of a prediction folder (apply_postprocessing_to_folder).
Input is a prediction folder plus a postprocessing.pkl -> postprocessed {CASE}{ending} label map

prediction_folder.description: Folder of {CASE}{ending} label maps (from nnunet_predict or nnunet_ensemble_predictions)

postprocessing_pkl_path.description: postprocessing.pkl written by nnunet_determine_postprocessing / nnunet_find_best_configuration (pickled (pp_fns, pp_fn_kwargs))

plans_json_path.description: plans.json of the model; '' = <prediction_folder>/plans.json (ensemble folders have none: give one member's plans.json)

output_dir.description: Base output directory; a fresh nnunet_apply_postprocessing_<timestamp>_<id> subdirectory is created per call (default: env NNUNET_OUTPUT_DIR or <project>/tmp/outputs)

nnunet_evaluate_predictions.description:
Score a folder of predicted segmentations against reference segmentations with nnU-Net's evaluator (per-case and mean Dice, IoU, TP/FP/FN/TN, n_pred/n_ref per label or region, foreground mean).
Input is a prediction folder, a reference folder and either dataset.json+plans.json (or a model folder) or

prediction_folder.description: Folder with predicted segmentations (e.g. a model's fold_X/validation folder or an nnUNetv2_predict output folder)

reference_folder.description: Folder with reference segmentations sharing file names and ending with the predictions (e.g. nnUNet_raw/<dataset>/labelsTr)

mode.description: dataset_plans = compute_metrics_on_folder2 (dataset.json + plans.json define labels/regions, ignore label and reader); simple = compute_metrics_on_folder_simple (explicit labels list, reader from the file ending); auto picks dataset_plans when dataset.json/plans.json are given or found (prediction folder, model_folder, or the model folder above a fold_X/validation folder) and simple when labels are given

dataset_json.description: Path to the dataset.json of the model (dataset_plans mode); give together with plans_json

plans_json.description: Path to the plans.json of the model (dataset_plans mode); give together with dataset_json

model_folder.description: Alternative to dataset_json/plans_json: a trained model folder (nnUNet_results/<dataset>/<trainer>__<plans>__<configuration>) whose dataset.json and plans.json are used

labels.description: Integer label ids to evaluate in simple mode (foreground labels, e.g. [1, 2]); ignored in dataset_plans mode

ignore_label.description: Simple mode only: label id in the reference that is excluded from all counts (dataset_plans mode takes it from dataset.json)

chill.description: If True, reference cases without a prediction are tolerated and only predicted cases are evaluated (upstream --chill); if False (upstream default) every reference case must have a prediction

num_processes.description: Worker processes of the spawn pool that reads and scores the cases (upstream default 8)

nnunet_raw.description: nnUNet_raw folder for the child process; default: env nnUNet_raw, else <project>/data/nnUNet_raw

nnunet_preprocessed.description: nnUNet_preprocessed folder for the child process; default: env nnUNet_preprocessed, else <project>/data/nnUNet_preprocessed

nnunet_results.description: nnUNet_results folder for the child process; default: env nnUNet_results, else <project>/data/nnUNet_results

output_dir.description: Base output directory; a fresh <tool>_<timestamp>_<id> subdirectory is created per call (default: env NNUNET_OUTPUT_DIR, else <project>/tmp/outputs)

nnunet_determine_postprocessing.description:
Determine nnU-Net's empirical postprocessing (removal of all but the largest connected component, for all foreground jointly and then per label/region) by testing whether each step improves the Dice against reference labels.
Input is a prediction folder with references and the model's plans.json/dat

prediction_folder.description: Folder with predicted segmentations for labelled cases (e.g. cross-validation predictions or an nnUNetv2_predict output of training cases)

reference_folder.description: Folder with the reference segmentations of these cases (same file names and ending), e.g. nnUNet_raw/<dataset>/labelsTr or nnUNet_preprocessed/<dataset>/gt_segmentations

plans_json.description: plans.json of the model that produced the predictions (may be given without dataset_json); default: the model_folder file, else <prediction_folder>/plans.json (written by nnUNetv2_predict)

dataset_json.description: dataset.json of the model (may be given without plans_json); default: the model_folder file, else <prediction_folder>/dataset.json

model_folder.description: Alternative to plans_json/dataset_json: a trained model folder (nnUNet_results/<dataset>/<trainer>__<plans>__<configuration>) whose plans.json and dataset.json are used

num_processes.description: Worker processes for applying candidate postprocessing steps and scoring (upstream default 8)

keep_postprocessed_files.description: Keep the postprocessed/ folder (postprocessed label maps + summary.json) next to the predictions; False deletes it after the decision

work_on_copy.description: If True, the segmentation files (+ dataset.json/plans.json) are copied into the fresh output directory and postprocessing is determined there, leaving the input folder untouched; if False (upstream behaviour) postprocessing.pkl, postprocessing.json, summary.json and postprocessed/ are written into prediction_folder itself

nnunet_raw.description: nnUNet_raw folder for the child process; default: env nnUNet_raw, else <project>/data/nnUNet_raw

nnunet_preprocessed.description: nnUNet_preprocessed folder for the child process; default: env nnUNet_preprocessed, else <project>/data/nnUNet_preprocessed

nnunet_results.description: nnUNet_results folder for the child process; default: env nnUNet_results, else <project>/data/nnUNet_results

output_dir.description: Base output directory; a fresh <tool>_<timestamp>_<id> subdirectory is created per call (default: env NNUNET_OUTPUT_DIR, else <project>/tmp/outputs)

nnunet_find_best_configuration.description:
Select nnU-Net's best configuration or pairwise ensemble by cross-validation foreground Dice (paper: empirical parameters) and determine its postprocessing, writing inference_information.json and inference_instructions.txt into nnUNet_results/<dataset>.
Input is a dataset with trained models (traine

dataset.description: Dataset id or name, e.g. '4', '004' or 'Dataset004_Hippocampus'

trainers.description: Trainer class names whose models are considered (upstream default nnUNetTrainer; short variants such as nnUNetTrainer_5epochs exist)

configurations.description: Configurations to consider; configurations absent from the plans file are skipped, configurations present in the plans must be trained for all requested folds (nnUNetv2_find_best_configuration default: 2d 3d_fullres 3d_lowres 3d_cascade_fullres)

plans_identifiers.description: Plans identifiers to consider (e.g. nnUNetPlans, nnUNetResEncUNetMPlans)

folds.description: Folds whose validation predictions are accumulated (upstream default 0 1 2 3 4); every requested fold must be trained for every considered model

allow_ensembling.description: Also evaluate every pairwise ensemble of the considered models (needs .npz validation probabilities: train/validate with export_validation_probabilities)

num_processes.description: Worker processes for accumulating, ensembling, scoring and postprocessing (upstream default 8)

overwrite.description: Recreate existing crossval_results_folds_* and ensemble folders (upstream default True); False reuses them, which may keep outdated results

strict.description: Upstream strict flag: raise if a considered model's output folder is missing instead of continuing (upstream API default False; the tool's own checks already require the folders)

nnunet_raw.description: nnUNet_raw folder (labelsTr is the reference for the accumulated cross-validation predictions); default: env nnUNet_raw, else <project>/data/nnUNet_raw

nnunet_preprocessed.description: nnUNet_preprocessed folder (plans files, gt_segmentations); default: env nnUNet_preprocessed, else <project>/data/nnUNet_preprocessed

nnunet_results.description: nnUNet_results folder holding the trained models; the tool WRITES into it (crossval_results_folds_*, ensembles/, inference_information.json, inference_instructions.txt); default: env nnUNet_results, else <project>/data/nnUNet_results

output_dir.description: Base output directory; a fresh <tool>_<timestamp>_<id> subdirectory is created per call (default: env NNUNET_OUTPUT_DIR, else <project>/tmp/outputs)

hdbet_extract_brain.description:
Skull-strip 3D MRI volumes with the HD-BET v2 nnU-Net model (brain mask and/or brain-extracted image).
Input is one .nii.gz file or a folder of .nii.gz files; output is per-case masks, skull-stripped images, QC overlay PNGs and a summary JSON in a fresh output directory.

input_path.description: 3D MRI NIfTI file (.nii.gz; T1w, contrast-enhanced T1w, T2w or FLAIR) or a folder whose *.nii.gz files are all brain-extracted

device.description: auto = CUDA device with the most free memory if >= 8 GiB free, else CPU with TTA disabled; cuda = most-free GPU; cpu = CPU only (about 1-2 min per volume without TTA)

use_tta.description: Test-time augmentation (mirroring along all axes, upstream default; inverse of the CLI --disable_tta); slightly better masks, ~8x slower, ignored on the auto->CPU fallback

save_mask.description: Keep the binary brain mask <case>_bet.nii.gz (uint8 {0,1}, input grid); CLI --save_bet_mask

save_brain_image.description: Write the skull-stripped image <case>.nii.gz (input voxels inside the mask, 0 outside); inverse of CLI --no_bet_image

output_dir.description: Base output directory; a fresh hdbet_extract_brain_<timestamp>_<id> subdirectory is created (default: HDBET_OUTPUT_DIR or <project>/tmp/outputs)

hdbet_apply_brain_mask.description:
Apply an existing brain mask to a co-registered image with HD-BET's apply_bet (voxels with mask == 0 are set to 0, header copied from the image).
Input is an image + mask NIfTI pair on one grid; output is the masked image .nii.gz plus a JSON summary (foreground voxels, volume, grid check).

image_path.description: 3D NIfTI (.nii/.nii.gz) image on the same voxel grid as the mask, e.g. a co-registered T2w/FLAIR/cT1w scan to skull-strip with the HD-BET mask of its T1w

mask_path.description: 3D NIfTI brain mask on the same grid (HD-BET *_bet.nii.gz or any mask); upstream keeps every voxel where the mask is non-zero

allow_geometry_mismatch.description: If true, a spacing/origin/direction difference beyond tolerance (1e-3 mm, 1e-2 mm, 1e-3) is only warned about and the mask is applied voxel-wise as upstream does; if false it is an error. Shape mismatch is always an error

output_dir.description: Base output directory; a fresh subdirectory is created per call (default: $HDBET_OUTPUT_DIR or <project>/tmp/outputs)

hdbet_inspect_brain_mask.description:
Quality-control a brain mask: foreground voxel count, volume (mm^3 and mL from spacing), bounding box, value set, connected components, and an overlay PNG of the slice with the most brain foreground (nnunetv2 plot_overlay).
Input is a mask NIfTI (optionally with its co-registered image); output is a

mask_path.description: 3D NIfTI brain mask (.nii/.nii.gz): HD-BET *_bet.nii.gz output, a reference mask, or a probability map

image_path.description: 3D NIfTI image on the same grid used for the overlay PNG (the slice with the most brain foreground, nnunetv2 plot_overlay); empty string = statistics only, no PNG

threshold.description: Foreground rule for masks whose values are not exactly {0,1}: voxels with value > threshold are brain; such masks are binarised to a uint8 copy before overlay and statistics. Ignored for {0,1} masks (foreground = mask != 0)

overlay_intensity.description: Upstream plot_overlay overlay_intensity: strength of the colour blend of the mask on the image slice (0.6 = upstream default)

three_views.description: Also render the same upstream slice selection/overlay along array axes 1 and 2 (adaptation composing upstream functions); the axis-0 PNG is always the exact plot_overlay output

output_dir.description: Base output directory; a fresh subdirectory is created per call (default: $HDBET_OUTPUT_DIR or <project>/tmp/outputs)

hdbet_evaluate_brain_mask.description:
Evaluate predicted brain mask(s) against reference mask(s): Dice, IoU, TP/FP/FN/TN and the maximum/average Hausdorff distance (mm); the paper's HD95 is not computed.
Input is a mask file+file or folder+folder pair on the same voxel grid; output is a per-case CSV, a summary JSON and per-case metrics.

prediction_path.description: Predicted brain mask: one .nii/.nii.gz file, or a folder of masks (e.g. an hdbet_extract_brain output folder)

reference_path.description: Reference (ground-truth) brain mask file, or a folder whose masks are paired with the predictions by basename

threshold.description: Voxels with value > threshold count as brain (label 1) in both masks; binary {0,1} masks are unchanged by the default 0.5

prediction_suffix.description: Suffix removed from prediction basenames before pairing, e.g. '_bet' for hd-bet folder outputs (<case>_bet.nii.gz vs <case>.nii.gz); '' pairs identical basenames

output_dir.description: Base output directory; a fresh subdirectory is created per call (default: HDBET_OUTPUT_DIR or <project>/tmp/outputs)
